full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Choudhury J:-This appeal by leave arises out of the judgment and order dated 6 January 1992 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division, Dhaka making the Rule absolute in Civil Revision No. 268 of 1989 and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 13 February 1988 of the Subordinate Judge in charge of the Court of the Additional District Judge, Narsigndi in Tide Appeal No. 14 of 1987 and restoring those dated July 1986 of the Munsif, Belabo in Tide Suit No.6 of 1985. In this appeal, defendant Nos.1-3 are the appellants while plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 are the respondent. 

 5. On consideration of the evidence the learned Munsif found the deed of heba-bil-ewaj to be genuine one. He then noticed utter discrepancy of evidence regarding the time, place and manner of execution of the disputed kabala and also the facts that the defendants refrained from getting the kabala registered till nearly 4 months of the alleged execution of the deed at; least through commission when Abdul Barek was critically ill. The learned Munsif therefore; found he circumstances of the execution of the disputed Kabala as extremely dubious. He father found that the Kabala after the death of Abdul Barek was presented by Abdul Motaleb, one of the recipients of the impugned Kabala who was not an heir to Abdul Barek on account of his mother being alive and that the deceased Abdul Barek left behind several heirs who, far from presenting the kabala in question for registration, were not been notified. The learned Munsif therefore came to the conclusion that the circumstances of the case indicated that the presentation of the kabala for registration was mala fide and therefore void. In the result the suit was decreed and the impugned kabala the declared as void and not binding on the plaintiffs. 

 6. Being aggrieved the contesting defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 14 of 1987. The appellate court while reversing the decree of the trial court did not even advert to the aforesaid reasoning of the trial court; nor did it discuss any evidence or reverse the material;  findings of the said court. Obviously the judgment of the appellate court was not in accordance with order XLI, Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 7. In revision, Civil Revision No. 268 of 1989, preferred by the plaintiffs the High Court Division after considering a certificate, as to Abdul Barek's date of death, not marked as an exhibit though held that Abdul Barek died on 24 October, 1983 which was sufficient to establish that the defendants brought their kabala into existence in a clandestine manner on false impersonation. Accordingly the said court set aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court and restored those of the trial court.
